notes:
Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private control plane for clinical triage chat and search. Primary motivation = predictable latency under 95th percentile SLAs, data residency and BYOK, and predictable unit economics for budgeting.

Key constraints and asks: 
- Must support VPC-only control plane; potential on-prem appliance for PHI-processing cluster.
- Required SLOs: p50 < 60ms generation for short intents (1-50 tokens), p95 < 400ms for chat turn (up to 512 tokens) for US-west region. Throughput target: sustained 120k tokens/sec across pool during business hours (peak), burst to 240k tokens/sec for 10% of time.
- Availability target: 99.95% monthly for dedicated pool; want SLA credits for violations and defined incident response times (1 hour initial, 4 hour mitigation window).
- Security: SOC2 + ISO27001 required, KMS BYOK, audit logs forwarded to Splunk, retention 7 years for audit trail.

Cost modeling discussion (notes from 2026-03-02 model walkthrough):
- Baseline compute shapes discussed: A100-class equivalent 1U GPU. We sketched three commit tiers: Small (8 GPUs), Mid (32 GPUs), Large (128 GPUs).
- Utilization assumptions (working model): effective service utilization = 60-70% after accounting for KV cache hit rates, short-tail chat, and maintenance/eviction. We recommended planning on conservative 60% for budget.
- Token throughput mapping: measured perf (proxy model) = ~1,100 tokens/sec per GPU at median prompt length/beam; with KV cache and batching, effective tokens/sec per GPU increases to ~1,600 tokens/sec during steady state. Use-case mix matters: embeddings and long-document searches reduce tokens/sec per GPU but increase memory.
- Unit economics snapshot (internal shorthand):
  * Committed cost basis (example Mid, 32 GPUs): committed monthly = $X (vendor quote placeholder); amortized per-GPU-month = committed/32.
  * Effective tokens/month = GPUs * tokens/sec * 3600*24*30 * utilization. Example with 32 GPUs, 1,600 t/s, 60% util -> ~2.6B tokens/month.
  * Unit cost per 1k tokens = (amortized infra + ops + license) / (effective tokens/month / 1000).
  * Sensitivity: moving utilization from 60% -> 75% lowers unit cost by ~20-25% in the model. Spike capacity priced as burst hours or spot; negotiate favorable burst credits in contract.
- GPU packing and model mix: plan two pools: chat-optimized (lower-latency, more frequent KV cache hits) and embed/semantic-search pool (larger batch-friendly jobs). This reduces overall reserved capacity needs by ~10-15% vs monolithic pool.

SLA/negotiation items raised by Verdant: 
- Request explicit p95 latency SLO by model family and sequence-length bucket; prefer per-route SLOs so triage routes get priority scheduling.
- Seeking credits for sustained p95 violations (not just downtime) and guaranteed mean time to rollback for canary rollouts.
- Want clarity on scheduled maintenance windows and ability to defer for major clinical events.
